stem.en: Two plates are moving apart. Which way does mantle rock move in the convection current below the gap?

text.en: It rises, then spreads out to both sides

feedback.en: Yes. Rising rock spreads under the plates and pulls them apart.

text.en: It sinks straight down into the deep mantle

feedback.en: No. Rock sinks where plates are drawn together.

text.en: It flows in from both sides towards the gap

feedback.en: No. Flow from both sides would draw the plates together.

text.en: It stays still, and only the plates move

feedback.en: No. Mantle rock moves very slowly in convection currents.

explanation.en: In a convection current, hot rock rises, spreads sideways under the plates and pulls them apart. Cooler rock sinks in another place, and there the plates are drawn together.

hints.en: Where in the loop does rock move sideways away from one line?
Think of hot dal reaching the top of the pot.
